_why: Indian grouping (decision D6) has two implementations, one per language, and neither can read the other. domain/money_text.py serves every PDF, email, 422 and log line; apps/web/lib/money/format.ts serves every screen. A CA reads both on one page — components/payroll/MonthlyReview.tsx renders formatPaise on a figure and the server's own sentence beside it — so a disagreement is visible in a single glance and was, until 24-09-2026, real: the backend used Python's own separator and grouped 1,23,456.78 as 123,456.78.
_the_unit_is_not_here: Neither side emits a currency symbol in these vectors, deliberately. A PDF writes 'Rs.' because ReportLab's core fonts carry no U+20B9 glyph; a screen and an email write the sign. The GROUPING is what both sides must agree on; the unit is the medium's.
_nothing_and_zero: The browser renders null/undefined as an em dash and Python renders None as nil, because their callers differ — a table cell with no figure is not a cell reading zero, while a PDF built from a row whose column is NULL must not fail the document. That divergence is deliberate and is asserted APART, in each suite, rather than being a vector here.

_whole_rupees_is_NOT_pinned_and_that_is_: domain.money_text.whole_rupees TRUNCATES toward zero — the year-end statements present in whole rupees and always have. lib/money/format.formatWhole does something DIFFERENT on purpose: where a figure carries paise it falls back to showing them, so an unrounded row stands out on a return-prep screen rather than being silently rounded in a browser (rounding it there would be a second implementation of CGST s.170, and the two disagree at exactly Rs x.50). Two rules for two callers, not a drift — so only the GROUPING is a parity vector. Harmonising them is the tempting mistake; each suite asserts its own side's rule separately.
